background-extraction.applyTo: The working image, every emission-line layer of the stack (Hα, OIII, SII or another line), or the image and every layer of the stack.
background-extraction.correction: Subtract removes an additive gradient (light pollution); divide removes a multiplicative one (vignetting), GraXpert only.
background-extraction.degree: Degree of the Siril polynomial, 1 to 4: 1 is a plane, higher bends with the gradient and may eat a large object.
background-extraction.dither: Siril RBF dithering of the model, against banding in smooth gradients; on by default.
background-extraction.engine: Which tool models the background: GraXpert's AI, Siril subsky RBF or a Siril polynomial; a missing tool greys its choice with the reason.
background-extraction.rbfSmooth: Siril RBF smoothing, 0 to 1; higher follows the gradient less closely; 0.5 by default.
background-extraction.samples: Siril RBF background samples per line; more follows a finer gradient; 30 by default.
background-extraction.smoothing: GraXpert smoothing of the model, 0 to 1; 0 keeps the model as GraXpert makes it, raise it when the model follows the object.
background-extraction.tolerance: Siril RBF sample rejection, in σ above the background: lower keeps samples off faint objects; 1.5 by default.
channel-combination.bBlack: Subtracted from the blue layer first, clipped at zero; 0 keeps it as stacked.
channel-combination.bSource: Which bundle layer fills the blue channel; a missing layer greys the choice, nothing replaces it.
channel-combination.bWeight: Multiplies the blue layer before combining; 1 keeps it as stacked.
channel-combination.gBlack: Subtracted from the green layer first, clipped at zero; 0 keeps it as stacked.
channel-combination.gSource: Which bundle layer fills the green channel; a missing layer greys the choice, nothing replaces it.
channel-combination.gWeight: Multiplies the green layer before combining; 1 keeps it as stacked.
channel-combination.lBlack: Subtracted from the luminance layer first, clipped at zero.
channel-combination.lOpacity: How much of the brightness comes from the luminance layer: 1 all of it, 0 none.
channel-combination.lSource: The layer that replaces the luminance, or none to keep the colour layers' own brightness.
channel-combination.lWeight: Multiplies the luminance layer before it is applied; 1 keeps it as stacked.
channel-combination.rBlack: Subtracted from the red layer first, clipped at zero; 0 keeps it as stacked.
channel-combination.rSource: Which bundle layer fills the red channel; a missing layer greys the choice, nothing replaces it.
channel-combination.rWeight: Multiplies the red layer before combining; 1 keeps it as stacked.
colour-balance.gainBlue: Multiplies the blue channel; the grey-region suggestion makes that region neutral. 1 changes nothing.
colour-balance.gainGreen: Multiplies the green channel; the grey-region suggestion makes that region neutral. 1 changes nothing.
colour-balance.gainRed: Multiplies the red channel; the grey-region suggestion makes that region neutral. 1 changes nothing.
colour-balance.offsetBlue: Added to the blue channel on linear data; the sky-region suggestion equalises the three medians.
colour-balance.offsetGreen: Added to the green channel on linear data; the sky-region suggestion equalises the three medians.
colour-balance.offsetRed: Added to the red channel on linear data; the sky-region suggestion equalises the three medians.
colour-calibration.bgTolAbove: How far above the background median, in σ, a pixel still counts as background.
colour-calibration.bgTolBelow: How far below the background median, in σ, a pixel still counts as background.
colour-calibration.catalogue: Where the stars come from: the local Gaia extract (offline), or Gaia online.
colour-calibration.enabled: Off, the step keeps the image as it is: what the dual-band profile ships, with its why.
colour-calibration.filter: The filter in front of the camera during the capture, as Siril names it. SPCC only.
colour-calibration.limitMag: The faintest catalogue star used; 0 lets Siril choose it from the field of view.
colour-calibration.method: SPCC fits the star colours with their Gaia spectra through your sensor and filter; PCC uses catalogue colours only.
colour-calibration.sensor: The camera sensor as Siril names it, usually the sensor behind your camera's model name. SPCC only.
colour-calibration.whiteReference: What counts as white: an average spiral galaxy for most targets, a G2V star for a solar white.
curves.blue: A curve on the blue channel only.
curves.green: A curve on the green channel only.
curves.luminance: A curve on the brightness, keeping the colour differences.
curves.red: A curve on the red channel only.
curves.rgb: One curve on the three channels; a straight line from (0, 0) to (1, 1) changes nothing.
curves.saturation: A curve on the HSL saturation: raise the middle to colour the nebula, not the noise.
denoise.amount: How much of the denoised image replaces the original, 0…1; 0 leaves it untouched.
denoise.chrominance: How much of the colour change is kept, 0…1: colour noise often takes more than the luminance.
denoise.luminance: How much of the brightness change is kept, 0…1: lower it to keep fine texture.
denoise.noise: The image noise σ in its own units (a few thousandths for a stack); thresholds are multiples of it; 0 removes nothing.
denoise.protectStars: Keeps what stands 5 to 10 noise levels above the plane's median (stars, bright cores) as it is.
denoise.scale1: Threshold at 1 px (the grain), in σ of the noise as it shows at that scale; 0 keeps it.
denoise.scale2: Threshold at 2 px, in σ of the noise as it shows at that scale; 0 keeps it.
denoise.scale3: Threshold at 4 px (blotches), in σ of the noise as it shows at that scale; 0 keeps it.
denoise.scale4: Threshold at 8 px (mottle), in σ of the noise as it shows at that scale; 0 keeps it.
emission-screens.haBackground: Where the Hα layer's median lands after its stretch; lower keeps the sky dark.
emission-screens.haBlack: The Hα layer's black point after its stretch: what lies below is hidden.
emission-screens.haBoost: Multiplies the Hα layer above 1 before screening; more exposure beats a stronger boost.
emission-screens.haContinuum: Subtracts k × the broadband red before screening, leaving the true Hα emission.
emission-screens.haContinuumK: The factor k of the broadband red taken away from Hα; 0 subtracts nothing.
emission-screens.haEnabled: Lays the Hα layer over the image; off leaves the colour image as it is.
emission-screens.haOpacity: How much the Hα layer brightens the image: 1 fully, 0 not at all.
emission-screens.haTint: The colour the Hα layer is screened in; red is the natural one.
emission-screens.linkLayers: Stretches the three layers with one curve; off stretches each from its own statistics.
emission-screens.nbBlend: How much of the screens is laid over the colour image: 1 all of them, 0 none.
emission-screens.oiiiBackground: Where the [OIII] layer's median lands after its stretch; lower keeps the sky dark.
emission-screens.oiiiBlack: The [OIII] layer's black point after its stretch: what lies below is hidden.
emission-screens.oiiiBoost: Multiplies the [OIII] layer above 1 before screening; more exposure beats a stronger boost.
emission-screens.oiiiContinuum: Subtracts k × the broadband green-blue before screening, leaving the true [OIII] emission.
emission-screens.oiiiContinuumK: The factor k of the broadband taken away from [OIII]; 0 subtracts nothing.
emission-screens.oiiiEnabled: Lays the [OIII] layer over the image; off leaves the colour image as it is.
emission-screens.oiiiOpacity: How much the [OIII] layer brightens the image: 1 fully, 0 not at all.
emission-screens.oiiiTint: The colour the [OIII] layer is screened in; teal is the natural one.
emission-screens.shadowsClip: Where each layer's shadows are cut, in σ of its noise below its median.
emission-screens.siiBackground: Where the [SII] layer's median lands after its stretch; lower keeps the sky dark.
emission-screens.siiBlack: The [SII] layer's black point after its stretch: what lies below is hidden.
emission-screens.siiBoost: Multiplies the [SII] layer above 1 before screening; more exposure beats a stronger boost.
emission-screens.siiContinuum: Subtracts k × the broadband red before screening, leaving the true [SII] emission.
emission-screens.siiContinuumK: The factor k of the broadband red taken away from [SII]; 0 subtracts nothing.
emission-screens.siiEnabled: Lays the [SII] layer over the image; off leaves the colour image as it is.
emission-screens.siiOpacity: How much the [SII] layer brightens the image: 1 fully, 0 not at all.
emission-screens.siiTint: The colour the [SII] layer is screened in; gold keeps it apart from Hα.
emission-screens.smooth: Blur in pixels applied to each layer before screening; 0 keeps the layer's grain.
emission-screens.starRadius: Opening radius in pixels: removes stars from each layer so only wide nebulosity is screened.
geometry.angle: A fine turn in degrees, clockwise, last; it resamples the pixels and removes the plate solution. 0 resamples nothing.
geometry.canvas: After a fine angle: keep the size (corners cut) or expand to hold the whole turned frame (black corners).
geometry.cropBottom: Rows removed at the bottom, in full-resolution pixels as the image is shown; 0 keeps them.
geometry.cropLeft: Columns removed on the left, in full-resolution pixels as the image is shown; 0 keeps them.
geometry.cropRight: Columns removed on the right, in full-resolution pixels as the image is shown; 0 keeps them.
geometry.cropTop: Rows removed at the top, in full-resolution pixels as the image is shown; 0 keeps them.
geometry.flipH: Mirrors left and right of the turned image: an exact copy, the plate solution follows.
geometry.flipV: Mirrors top and bottom of the turned image: an exact copy, the plate solution follows.
geometry.interpolation: How a fine angle resamples: bilinear is soft, bicubic sharper, Lanczos-3 the sharpest with slight ringing.
geometry.rotation: Quarter turns clockwise, after the crop: exact pixel copies, the plate solution follows.
hdr.enabled: Compresses the smooth bright core on linear data, before the stretch; off changes nothing.
hdr.kneeAboveSky: How far above the bundle sky the compression starts, absolute; the default 0.00084 sits just above a dark sky's noise.
hdr.openRadius: Opening radius in pixels that removes stars before the smooth light is measured, avoiding dark rings.
hdr.sigma: The scale in pixels below which detail is left alone: only the smooth light is compressed.
hdr.softness: The width s of the asinh roll-off above the knee, absolute; the default 0.00118 rolls a galaxy core off without a hard edge.
levels.bHighlights: The white point: values at or above it become white; 1 keeps every highlight. Blue channel only, when unlinked.
levels.bMidtones: The midtone balance: below 0.5 brightens, above darkens; 0.5 changes nothing. Blue channel only, when unlinked.
levels.bShadows: The black point: values at or below it become black. Set it just below the histogram foot. Blue channel only, when unlinked.
levels.gHighlights: The white point: values at or above it become white; 1 keeps every highlight. Green channel only, when unlinked.
levels.gMidtones: The midtone balance: below 0.5 brightens, above darkens; 0.5 changes nothing. Green channel only, when unlinked.
levels.gShadows: The black point: values at or below it become black. Set it just below the histogram foot. Green channel only, when unlinked.
levels.linked: One triple (RGB/K) for the three channels; off, each channel first takes its own triple, then the RGB/K one.
levels.outputHigh: The level the white point is mapped to; 1 keeps full white.
levels.outputLow: The level the black point is mapped to; 0 keeps true black.
levels.rHighlights: The white point: values at or above it become white; 1 keeps every highlight. Red channel only, when unlinked.
levels.rMidtones: The midtone balance: below 0.5 brightens, above darkens; 0.5 changes nothing. Red channel only, when unlinked.
levels.rShadows: The black point: values at or below it become black. Set it just below the histogram foot. Red channel only, when unlinked.
levels.rgbHighlights: The white point: values at or above it become white; 1 keeps every highlight.
levels.rgbMidtones: The midtone balance: below 0.5 brightens, above darkens; 0.5 changes nothing.
levels.rgbShadows: The black point: values at or below it become black. Set it just below the histogram foot.
line-injection.haBlack: Subtracted from the Hα excess before adding it (its sky level): what lies below adds nothing, the rest drops by as much.
line-injection.haBlue: The share of the Hα excess that goes into the blue plane, 0…1.
line-injection.haContinuumK: The factor k of the broadband plane named in the suggestion, taken from Hα before adding it; too high hollows the stars.
line-injection.haGain: How much of the Hα excess is added to the base, 0…4; 0 adds nothing.
line-injection.haGreen: The share of the Hα excess that goes into the green plane, 0…1.
line-injection.haRed: The share of the Hα excess that goes into the red plane, 0…1.
line-injection.oiiiBlack: Subtracted from the [OIII] excess before adding it (its sky level): what lies below adds nothing, the rest drops by as much.
line-injection.oiiiBlue: The share of the [OIII] excess that goes into the blue plane, 0…1.
line-injection.oiiiContinuumK: The factor k of the broadband plane named in the suggestion, taken from [OIII] before adding it; too high hollows the stars.
line-injection.oiiiGain: How much of the [OIII] excess is added to the base, 0…4; 0 adds nothing.
line-injection.oiiiGreen: The share of the [OIII] excess that goes into the green plane, 0…1.
line-injection.oiiiRed: The share of the [OIII] excess that goes into the red plane, 0…1.
line-injection.siiBlack: Subtracted from the [SII] excess before adding it (its sky level): what lies below adds nothing, the rest drops by as much.
line-injection.siiBlue: The share of the [SII] excess that goes into the blue plane, 0…1.
line-injection.siiContinuumK: The factor k of the broadband plane named in the suggestion, taken from [SII] before adding it; too high hollows the stars.
line-injection.siiGain: How much of the [SII] excess is added to the base, 0…4; 0 adds nothing.
line-injection.siiGreen: The share of the [SII] excess that goes into the green plane, 0…1.
line-injection.siiRed: The share of the [SII] excess that goes into the red plane, 0…1.
plate-solve.catalogue: Where the stars come from: the local Gaia extract (offline, just download-catalogues), or Gaia online.
plate-solve.dec: The approximate image centre, declination: degrees as +41 16 09, or one number. Empty until you type or take one.
plate-solve.focalMm: The focal length of the optics, in millimetres; with the pixel size it gives the scale Siril looks for.
plate-solve.limitMag: The faintest catalogue star used; 0 lets Siril choose it from the field of view.
plate-solve.pixelSizeUm: The camera pixel size, in micrometres; suggested from the capture header when it carries one.
plate-solve.ra: The approximate image centre, right ascension: hours as 00 42 44, or degrees as one number. Empty until you type or take one.
saturation.amount: How much the colour is raised, in HSL; 0 changes nothing.
saturation.bandHigh: Lightness where the boost applies fully.
saturation.bandLow: Lightness where the boost starts to apply.
saturation.highlightFloor: The fraction of the boost still applied at white: 1 keeps it all, 0 none.
saturation.lumaDesat: How much of the colour is kept: 1 changes nothing, 0 blends every pixel to its luminance.
saturation.masked: Limits the boost to a lightness band, so the sky's chroma noise and the star cores stay protected.
saturation.rolloffStart: Lightness above which the boost rolls off toward the highlights.
saturation.starDesat: How much the bright star cores are sent toward white, so they do not become coloured discs.
saturation.starDesatHigh: Lightness where the star-core desaturation applies fully.
saturation.starDesatLow: Lightness where the star-core desaturation starts.
sky-desat.coreGuardPx: Pixels of guard around bright star cores, never treated.
sky-desat.coreLevel: Brightness relative to the sky above which a pixel counts as a star core.
sky-desat.floorHigh: Brightness relative to the sky where the sky floor is fully treated.
sky-desat.floorLow: Brightness relative to the sky where the sky floor starts to be treated.
sky-desat.keepCool: Flattens only the warm (brown, olive) patches; use on reflection fields, off on emission fields.
sky-desat.nebulaHigh: Brightness relative to the sky where bright extended signal keeps all its colour.
sky-desat.nebulaLow: Brightness relative to the sky where bright extended signal starts to keep its colour.
sky-desat.scalePx: The scale in pixels of the mottle treated: structures smaller than this keep their colour.
sky-desat.starDetailPx: Pixels of fine detail around stars left untouched.
sky-desat.starHigh: Brightness relative to the sky where the star mask protects fully.
sky-desat.starLow: Brightness relative to the sky where the star mask starts to protect.
sky-desat.strength: How much the faint sky is greyed: 0 changes nothing, 1 removes all its colour.
star-recomposition.chroma: The star colour, from grey (0) to the original (1); at 0.25 red giants stop looking orange.
star-recomposition.mode: Additive adds the star layer back; screen blends it so bright cores do not clip.
star-recomposition.presence: How much of the stars come back: 1 keeps them all, 0.25 leaves only a hint.
stretch.asinhBlack: The level taken as black before the asinh stretch.
stretch.asinhStretch: Strength β of the asinh stretch, which keeps each pixel's colour ratios; 0 changes nothing.
stretch.ghsHighlights: Above this level the GHS curve stays linear, protecting the highlights.
stretch.ghsIntensity: Shape b of the GHS curve: how much the stretch concentrates around the symmetry point.
stretch.ghsShadows: Below this level the GHS curve stays linear, protecting the shadows.
stretch.ghsStretch: Strength of the generalised hyperbolic stretch, ln(D+1); 0 changes nothing.
stretch.ghsSymmetry: The level the GHS curve lifts around; put it near the signal to bring up.
stretch.headroom: The ceiling star cores roll off below, so they keep colour instead of clipping white; 1 is off.
stretch.linked: One curve for the three channels, keeping the colour balance; off stretches each channel on its own.
stretch.mode: The curve of the first non-linear step: MTF (Siril autostretch), GHS, or asinh.
stretch.shadowsClip: Where the shadows are cut, in σ of the noise below the background median; Siril uses −2.8.
stretch.targetBackground: Where the background median lands after the stretch, 0…1; Siril uses 0.25.
